practices.trigger: A rollout interrupts accepted long-running jobs or exhausts a retry budget.
practices.failure_mode: Retiring generations repeatedly reclaim work; an effect is replayed or an old owner overwrites its successor.
practices.mechanism: Close authoritative generation admission, reconcile owned/reserved work, persist compatible continuation and receipts, fence mutation and cleanup, keep distinct maintenance and business counters.
practices.applicability_limits: Requires enforceable admission, durable progress, compatible capacity and a protected-effect contract. Local process/PostgreSQL checks do not prove Kubernetes, broker or external effect behavior.
practices.counterexample: An empty local task set omits a receive in flight; readiness alone does not stop queue admission.
practices.verification: Force A/B/C retirement, real signals, effect-before-checkpoint death, paused-owner resumption, mixed readers/writers, bounded expiry and owned resource cleanup.

practices.trigger: A delayed cache fill or backfill overlaps update or delete/recreate.
practices.failure_mode: A replacement reuses the numeric revision, or old payload is relabeled with a new token from a different snapshot.
practices.mechanism: Read payload/incarnation/revision coherently and publish through an atomic guard on non-reused incarnation plus revision.
practices.applicability_limits: The authority must expose/enforce these semantics; numeric counters without durable identity do not prevent ABA.
practices.counterexample: revision=1 identifies both a deleted row and its replacement.
practices.verification: Pause between capture/publication, mutate or recreate, assert the full final identity/value set independently and retry on the new snapshot.

practices.trigger: Concurrent replicas make business decisions before reconciling.
practices.failure_mode: Converged state violates an invariant or repeats an irreversible effect.
practices.mechanism: Test merging locally valid states against the invariant; coordinate or allocate enforceable rights at the actual decision/effect boundary where necessary.
practices.applicability_limits: Merge algebra alone supplies neither freshness nor crash-safe external effects.
practices.counterexample: Two unique sales converge as a set while exceeding stock of one.
practices.verification: Force both local decisions, both merge orders and duplicate delivery; check stock/effect counts with an independent oracle.

practices.trigger: A schema or derived representation evolves during mixed writer generations and backfill.
practices.failure_mode: Old-only writes invalidate new-only reads; one shard publishes early; rollback cannot represent post-switch writes.
practices.mechanism: Require all-writer atomic revision maintenance or another enforceable protocol, gate all required shards/coverage/catch-up/exposure separately, retain a compatible bridge or restore fallback before old-only admission.
practices.applicability_limits: F1 maintenance phases are historical engine-specific protocols; actual engines have distinct publication/revert contracts. Cross-store writes need their own partial-success repair.
practices.counterexample: Equal source/derived row counts hide one missing identity and one resurrected row.
practices.verification: Compare complete expected and actual sets both directions; force a delayed old commit, partial shard completion and rollback after new writes.

practices.trigger: Long jobs, prefetch or dependency fanout starve other tenants.
practices.failure_mode: Fair next-delivery ordering and active-only limits leave no physical capacity for quiet work.
practices.mechanism: Account for all resident ownership and protected dependency budgets; reserve capacity and permit borrowing only with a feasible bounded reclaim/settlement contract.
practices.applicability_limits: Nonpreemptible work cannot release capacity merely on cancellation request; placement/admission/delivery/runtime fairness differ.
practices.counterexample: Idle CPU coexists with four owned connection/worker slots, so quiet work misses its deadline.
practices.verification: Record fixed arrivals, all ownership states, actual release and per-tenant completion/deadline outcomes over a common horizon.

practices.trigger: Budgets cross hosts/serialization or cancellation affects resource cleanup.
practices.failure_mode: A fresh hop timeout renews caller lifetime; a wall-clock deadline is used in an event-loop domain; a cancelled child still owns a released connection.
practices.mechanism: Preserve remaining operation budget with an explicit transport/time authority and separate cancellation request, caller completion, work termination and owned resource release.
practices.applicability_limits: Some local processes share a monotonic clock; its origin is not host/reboot portable. Runtime suspend and cancellation contracts must be checked.
practices.counterexample: Task.cancel returns before cleanup, then another task reuses the same active connection.
practices.verification: Force representation/wall/skew boundaries, earlier parent expiry, delayed handoff and slow cancellation; observe actual resource release and useful subsequent work.
